name: sol_defi_lending_7
description: Liquidation incentive scales purely with position size, leaving small positions unprofitable to liquidate
question: The source file in `source` implements a liquidation function that computes the liquidator's reward as a fixed percentage or proportional fraction of the position's collateral/debt size, with no minimum incentive floor or gas-cost-covering bonus, so that positions below a certain size yield a liquidation reward smaller than the cost of liquidating them, causing small unhealthy positions to be economically unprofitable to liquidate and accumulate as bad debt, excluding designs that apply a fixed minimum bonus, flat liquidation fee, or otherwise guarantee liquidators a profitable payout regardless of position size.
criteria: liquidate() pays the liquidator collateral*bonusRate with no minimum floor amount added, so tiny positions yield near-zero reward
calculateLiquidationIncentive() returns debtRepaid * liquidationBonusBps / 10000 without any base/flat bonus term
the liquidation reward formula scales strictly linearly with position size and has no clamping to a minimum reward value
small positions can be left unliquidated indefinitely because the code provides no mechanism (subsidy, minimum bounty, batching) to make their liquidation profitable
